meta.title: Symmetric vs Asymmetric: Solving Key Exchange

views.label: 1. The shared-secret problem
views.note: Both sides need the same key K — but moving K over a public wire is exactly where it leaks.

views.label: 2. Publish the public key
views.note: A public key is like a padlock with your name on it — anyone can take it and lock mail to you.

views.label: 3. Private key never travels
views.note: Only the private key can unlock. It never leaves its owner.

messages.label: "we both need the same secret key K"
"so how do we hand K over safely?"
messages.note: every hop on the wire can read the mail

messages.label: "the wire is public — K could be copied"
"here is my PUBLIC key — take it"
messages.note: public key encrypts — safe to travel in the open

messages.label: "I lock my message with your public key"
"my PRIVATE key unlocks it — never leaves me"

cards.title: Symmetric vs asymmetric
items: Symmetric: the same key on both sides — fast, but sharing the key is the catch
Asymmetric: a public / private pair — public encrypts, only private decrypts
The public key can travel in the open; the private key never leaves its owner
Real systems use asymmetric to agree the secret key, then symmetric for speed
